explanation: Recalculation gives nullities 16−9=7 and 16−8=8, so an adapted chain basis has 8−7=1 rank-5 vector (d). The earlier uncertainty concerns the unspecified basis, not the arithmetic. Let v have rank 5 and let u₁,…,u₇ form a basis of ker((D−3I)⁴). Both {u₁,…,u₇,v} and {v,u₁+v,…,u₇+v} are generalized eigenvector bases of the eigenvalue-3 subspace, but they contain respectively 1 and 8 rank-5 vectors. Thus d is the intended answer, while the literal question does not determine a unique count.
